x: Leyline is a free, open-source mod launcher and peer-to-peer realm network . Anyone can host a realm in one click, from the browser or the desktop; players find it on the shared realm list and join, and mods come along. Try it now on the Dalaran Hangout , Leyline's sample realm. Note: Leyline is a fan project. It isn't affiliated with or endorsed by Blizzard, it sells nothing, and it never ships Blizzard's game files. This manual also covers the classic Leyline Launcher , the earlier desktop app, which existing players still use.

The launcher checks for updates by itself and ignores anything that isn't signed by Leyline's release key or is older than what you have. Updates download quietly in the background ("Downloading update 42%"), are checked against their fingerprint, and then a gold UPDATE READY · RESTART button appears above PLAY. Updating replaces only program files: your addons, settings, realms and screenshots are never touched. If an update fails, it says so and tries again next time (details in Logs\update.log ).

Your data folder is %LOCALAPPDATA%\OpenVanilla for the installer (an install from before the rename keeps its older data folder), or the folder beside OpenVanilla.exe for the zip. In the launcher, Realms → Realm browser shows the live directory, filterable by type, template and free room, plus your favourites and recent realms. Realms come in groups: Group Meaning Verified realms · Official Run by Leyline Verified realms · Vetted Checked by the maintainers Community P2P realms Hosted by players; not vetted, play at your own risk The Leyline realm list shows the realms on the Leyline network.

Realms → My servers → Add a server : name, host or IP, port (default 3724 ), the realm's website (optional) and which client to use. Each row shows its ping, with Select , Website and Remove . The Community list has hand-picked servers with a Play here button. Using a stock client without the launcher? Put set realmlist <address> in the client's realmlist.wtf .

A friend hosting a realm can send you an invite link. Paste it in the Invite link box and press Join invite , or just click it: Windows hands it to the launcher. Before you join, the launcher shows what kind of connection it is. Join by address takes an address ( host:port ) and optionally a guest code, account and password. Note: Peer-to-peer invites, the relay and the community directory are built and tested but switch on later. Until then, add friends' servers by address.

Connection Your IP Notes Through the relay (recommended) Hidden Traffic passes through Leyline's relay, end-to-end encrypted Direct The host sees it Sign-in details between friends travel unencrypted; only join hosts you trust LAN Same network Leyline isn't involved at all The launcher remembers a host's key the first time you join. If it changes, it warns you ("Host key changed … ask them for a new invite link"): someone may be pretending to be them.
The classic launcher's volunteer node network never left its test round and is retired. Leyline's network carries players to hosts for you.

Leyline's network is built so anyone can host a realm and anyone can find and join it safely. It has five parts: Part Runs on What it does The host The host's PC (or Leyline's servers for official realms) Runs the whole world: every player, creature, bot and spell The directory Leyline's server Lists realms by tier, checks they're reachable, tells your launcher how to reach them Relays Leyline's servers Carry traffic for hosts behind home routers, hiding both sides' IP addresses Nodes Volunteers' PCs Extra relays: more connections, attack absorption, shorter routes One sign-in Leyline's server

t: Why there isn't one giant world
x: A realm's whole world runs in one server program on one machine; on the server Leyline uses, each continent is updated by a single processor core. Relays and nodes add connections , not world power: they can't run part of someone's world, and letting volunteers do that would let them hand out items or read everyone's chat. So Leyline grows in two ways at once: The official realm gets faster: measured tuning, then splitting each continent into regions that run in parallel (the approach Nostalrius used), and copies ("layers") only for launches and big events. The network gets wider: more realms,
Want to be the one with the realm? See Host your own realm .

Play Solo runs a complete Vanilla realm on your own PC: the SPP Classics server with playerbots , computer-controlled characters who join your group for dungeons and group quests and roam the world. It listens only on your own PC and works offline once it's set up. Good to know Needs Windows 10/11 64-bit, your own Vanilla Client v1.3 (English, build 5875), a few GB of disk (SSD helps), 8 GB+ RAM recommended Internet Only for the first download and updates Characters Stay on your PC: they can't move to or from online realms Players None: no trading, guilds or chat with people Vanilla Remastered

In the launcher, switch Home to SOLO and press PLAY . It downloads the solo server (about 110 MB, then about 700 MB of server files). Both resume if interrupted. The server's setup window opens once: type 1 , wait for the Vanilla menu, then type 0 . PLAY turns ready by itself: READY · SOLO ON THIS PC . Already have SPP Classics? Choose I have SPP Classics… and point the launcher at it.
Press PLAY in Solo mode. The launcher starts the database, login and world servers hidden in the background and logs you in as SOLO / SOLO . Closing the game saves the world and stops the servers.

Playerbots fill the world and will group with you. Ask them to follow, attack or assist in party chat, or let Herald play your own character ( /herald , see In-game features ): Play Solo has Herald's self-bot switched on.

It's your realm: you can change XP rates, add NPCs and give yourself GM powers. The config lives under Realms\Solo\...\mangosd.conf . The easiest way is to ask an AI agent with the starter prompts in Connect an AI , or by hand in Edit your own game . Back up first.

The short version of privacy.html : No ads, no analytics, nothing sold. The realm stores a password verifier, never your password. The launcher can remember your password encrypted with Windows' own protection, and sends no crash reports or files. Sign in with Discord only gets your identity and permission to add you to the server; it never sees your Discord password or messages. Herald keeps your Discord ID and name, your join and gate dates and your adventurer number. You must be 13 or older. To delete your data, ask on Discord. t: Test without starting the game: the Lua sim
x: The repo's Lua sim runs addons in a fake Vanilla client in seconds, with the Lua 5.0 rules enforced. It loads addons from Data/Interface/AddOns/ in a checkout of the repo, so put your addon folder there to test it. lua5.1 devkit/sim/run_tests.lua # every test lua5.1 devkit/sim/run_tests.lua persona # only tests matching "persona" SIM_VERBOSE=1 lua5.1 devkit/sim/run_tests.lua Results are PASS , FAIL and XFAIL (a known bug that's still there). A test lives in devkit/sim/tests/<addon>.lua : T.test("hello prints a greeting", function() local env = T.addon("MyFirstAddon") env.__slash("/hello") T.ha

devkit\Dev.bat has a menu for everything: Option What it does Quick checks py -3 devkit\check.py : repo sanity, including refusing game files Addon tests The Lua sim SQL tests Realm database changes, in Docker or locally Dev proxy http://localhost:8080 is the live realm, but the page scripts and Vanilla Remastered addons come from your folder. Nothing is pushed. Herald Lite A headless test bot running scenarios in devkit/heraldlite/scenarios/ Measure loading How fast the browser client loads Rebuild patch-Z The client patch, in Docker

t: Realm rules on your own server
x: On a realm you host (or Play Solo), the rules are yours. Rates (XP, drops, rested, honor) live in mangosd.conf : Solo's is under Realms\Solo\...\mangosd.conf , a hosted realm's under Realms\Hosted\custom\mangosd.conf . Change a line, save, restart the world server. Vanilla Remastered switches are lines in the same file, set to 1 (on) or 0 (off): Setting Does OpenVanilla.AutoLearn Learn trainer spells on level-up OpenVanilla.FreeRespec Free talent resets OpenVanilla.DualSpec Two specs from level 10 OpenVanilla.StarterPet Hunters start with a pet (official realm: 0) OpenVanilla.AoeLoot , OpenVan

t: Models and mounts: the Model Porter
x: The Model Porter turns a modern model into one the Vanilla client can show, and adds it to your realm as a creature or rideable mount. Run tools\modelport\Model_Porter.bat ; it opens http://127.0.0.1:8765 . (Command line: python tools/modelport model.glb --name Gryphon --kind mount --add .) Feed it a glTF/glb , or a modern .m2 with its .skin , .skel , .anim and .blp files. For a mount, name the rider's node Seat (or Saddle ); animations are matched by name (Idle, Walk, Run...). Test in game as a GM: .additem , .npc add , .modify morph , .demorph . Limits: up to 254 bones; models over 21,845 tr

The Vanilla Remastered windows, icons and frames are drawn by scripts in tools/ ( gen_*_art.py , sharing tools/artkit.py ). Each writes a .tga for the Vanilla client and a .blp for the browser client; sizes must be powers of two. tools/png_to_blp.py converts your own PNGs.

The Vanilla Remastered addons, art, loading screens, custom models and two race/class tables ship to clients in one small archive, patch-Z.MPQ . It isn't in the repo: build it with python3 tools/sync_patchz.py --dbc-dir DIR , where DIR holds your own 1.12.1 client's CharBaseInfo.dbc and SkillRaceClassInfo.dbc (the repo keeps only our changes to them, in realm/classicplus/dbc_deltas/ ). Without --dbc-dir it builds the archive without those tables. The realm builds its own ( hetzner/openvanilla_build_patchz.sh ). --check only reports what would change.
When it works, share it: Publish to the Workshop .

c: Connect an AI to your game
x: The Assistant addon puts the same prompts inside the game, so you can grab one without alt-tabbing. Open it with /assistant (or /ai ), or the Assistant button in the Esc menu. /assistant how opens the how-to tab. Prompts tab: pick a prompt; its text is selected in the box, press Ctrl+C to copy (the Vanilla client has no clipboard button), then paste into your agent. How it works tab: the five steps on this page, short. The Assistant never talks to an AI or the network. Its footer says so: the AI runs outside the game, in its own window, on your PC.

c: Connect an AI to your game
x: These are written into CLAUDE.md , and you should hold the agent to them: Your PC only. It works in your Leyline folder and your own server folders. t: Herald Autopilot is not an AI
c: Connect an AI to your game
x: Herald Autopilot (the desktop app started with Herald Autopilot.bat , and Let Herald play / /herald in game) can play your character, but it isn't a language model: it drives the realm's own playerbot "self-bot" with rules and a gear simulator. It does not hide from staff (no anti-ban tricks, no fake human delays), and on the official realm autoplay is currently switched off. Learning is opt-in and sends anonymous numbers only. More in Community: Herald .

t: For realm staff: AI in moderation
c: Connect an AI to your game
x: Hosts can optionally let an AI model help sort player reports in Herald. It reads the report and the chat lines and suggests a score and an action; the AI never kicks or bans, humans decide . It's off unless the host sets MOD_AI_URL , MOD_AI_KEY and MOD_AI_MODEL (any OpenAI-compatible endpoint) in Herald's server settings. The key stays on the realm server; players never need one.

On the website: open the Workshop , pick an addon, press Install . It opens the launcher, which downloads the package, checks its fingerprint and installs it into AddOns\Enabled . Collections install several at once. In the launcher: Workshop → Addons . Installed lists yours, with Enable/Disable each. From a zip: Workshop → Installed → Install from .zip . It accepts plain addon zips, packs of several addons and GitHub "Download ZIP" archives, renames folders to match their .toc , and refuses anything that would land outside your AddOns folder. From GitHub: in Advanced mode, the GitHub tab sear

It runs on Vanilla. ## Interface: 11200 in the .toc , Lua 5.0 only ( the rules ), folder name = .toc name. It passes the scanner: python3 tools/workshop_scan.py MyAddon --json ( details ). Aim for works . It has a licence that lets others share it , as a LICENSE file in the folder. The Workshop can host copies only under: MIT, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, GPL-2.0, GPL-3.0, LGPL-2.1, LGPL-3.0, MPL-2.0, Unlicense, CC0-1.0. It's yours to share. You wrote it, or its licence allows sharing and you credit the author. Screenshots and a one-line summary ready. An AI agent can draft the list

On the Workshop page , Share an addon (signed in): Field Limit Addon name 48 characters One line 280 characters Licence One from the list above Source link Optional, https Zip The addon folder with its .toc and licence, up to 10 MB Tick I wrote this addon, or its licence lets anyone share it, and the licence file is in the zip , and send. You'll see "Upload #n is in the review queue". You can upload five a day, with at most five waiting. Note: Uploads open with the realm update that adds them. Until then, use a catalogue entry .

Every upload is scanned in the fake Vanilla client before a person looks at it. The scanner flags anything that sends chat when it loads or on a timer, reads other addons' saved data, uses os or io , moves gold or items, or runs arbitrary code. Anything serious holds the upload for a moderator. Uploads are never served to players until a moderator approves them; approved ones become catalogue entries.

The Workshop's source is one file per addon in workshop/catalog/<id>.yml in the repo. Adding yours by pull request: id: my-theme # lowercase, digits, dashes; 2-48 characters name: MyTheme author: You summary: A dark, minimal skin for the Vanilla Remastered windows. description: | What it does, how to open it (/mytheme), what to expect. category: interface # interface, unitframes, combat, raid, quests, bags, maps, # social, economy, professions, macros, tooltips, utility, classicplus tags: [theme, minimal] license: MIT rehost: true source_url: https://github.com/you/MyTheme homepage: https://gi
Add one of these topics to your GitHub repo: wow-vanilla-addon , vanilla-wow-addon or turtle-wow . The indexer finds tagged repos, and a person reviews each before it's listed.

t: Port an open addon into Vanilla Remastered
x: Vanilla Remastered addons get the suite's settings window and look. To wrap an openly licensed addon: python3 tools/workshop_port.py path\to\SomeAddon --license MIT --name SomeAddonPlus --author "You" --source https://... It writes workshop/ports/<Folder>Plus/ (a .toc , a Lua file and PORT_NOTES.txt ), refuses addons without an allowed licence, and never publishes anything by itself. Test it in the sim and the game, then upload it.

A collection is a curated list of addons for a play style (raiders, roleplayers...), installed with one click. They live in workshop/collections/<id>.yml : id , name , curator , summary , description , banner and addons: [ids] . Send one by pull request.
Signed-in players can rate and review addons on each addon's page. Moderators can hide a review's text if it breaks the rules. Install counts are anonymous.

t: List a fork, repo or project
x: Forks of Leyline, other clients, server projects, repacks and games built on the same tech go in the Projects directory ( www/community/directory.json ). Each gets a page at project.html#<id> and a spot in the launcher's Workshop → Projects tab. To be listed, open an issue with the name, link, a short description, the credits and a screenshot. An entry looks like this: { "id": "my-fork", "name": "My Fork", "kind": "source", "client": "1.12.1", "version": "0.3", "author": "You", "license": "MIT", "tags": ["fork", "pvp"], "url": "https://github.com/you/my-fork", "homepage": "https://you.example"

Fork the repo on GitHub ( orionopenwow/Leyline-Launcher ) or clone it to another host. Keep the credits. Leyline is built on benilla (MIT / Apache-2.0); keep its licence files and credit line. Keep the game's own files out. The repo's checks refuse them, and so should your fork: players bring their own Vanilla Client v1.3. Rename it. Use your own name and art; don't present your fork as the official Leyline. Point it at your own realm. Realm addresses live in the launcher's defaults and the site's config; your fork's players should never sign in to a realm you don't run. List it in the Project

Report bugs in the Discord's bug-reports forum or as GitHub issues , with your logs ( Logs\ in the launcher's data folder). Make addons and publish them . Stream and make videos : link your channel . Host a realm or run a node . Fix the manual (next). Send code : see below.

This manual is plain text in the repo: one Markdown file per chapter in docs/manual/ . To fix or add something: Edit the chapter's .md file. Sections are ## Heading {#link-id} ; keep existing ids so links keep working. Build it: python tools/build_manual.py --check . It writes the pages to www/manual/ and fails if any link or anchor is broken. Send it as a pull request, or describe the change in an issue. An AI agent with the workspace kit can do this for you: "Read CLAUDE.md. In docs/manual/, add a section about <topic> to the right chapter, then run the build with --check."

** main ** is where work happens. ** stable ** is what's live: the realm, the website and the launcher's updates all follow it. Only releases move it.

py -3 devkit\check.py # repo checks (CI runs --strict) lua5.1 devkit/sim/run_tests.lua # addon tests python devkit/db/test_sql.py --local # realm database changes py -3 -m pytest tests # launcher, site, bot, tools When you fix a bug, add a test that would have caught it: addon bugs in devkit/sim/tests/<addon>.lua , server or SQL bugs in devkit/db/test_sql.py or a Herald Lite scenario.

A release is playtested on staging, gets a ## New in X.Y.Z section in CHANGELOG.md , and is tagged by the maintainer. The build server makes the installer, the zip, their checksums and a signed update manifest; launchers pick it up by themselves.

No game files, ever: checks refuse MPQs, DBCs and stock interface files. No secrets in commits: tokens, keys and passwords stay in .env files that git ignores. Keep it free: nothing that sells power, items or game time.
Launcher: Settings → Folders → Open logs . The files that matter are launcher.log , update.log and web-backend.log . Attach them to a bug report (they don't contain your password).

Is this official? # No. Leyline is a free fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Blizzard. World of Warcraft is a trademark of Blizzard Entertainment, Inc. Does it cost anything? # No. Leyline is free, and nothing in it is for sale. Why do I need my own 1.12.1 game client? # Leyline never distributes the game's files and never downloads a client.
